This is factually accurate and specific to new code in the diff. It is not a demonstrable defect (the admin controller's removeMember action ignores the return value, so no incorrect behavior is observable there), but it is a legitimate, concrete promise-chaining concern for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that not returning the promise from findMembers() in the success handler is a bug that leaves stale members displayed. However, looking at the code, the removeMember function DOES return the Discourse.ajax promise (line 43-49), and the .then() callback calls self.findMembers() which will update the members. Whether or not the inner findMembers() promise is returned from the .then() callback doesn't affect whether the UI gets updated - findMembers() will still execute and update the model's members property. The UI will reflect the new state. Not chaining the inner promise only affects what the caller receives, but in the action handler (removeMember action in the controller), the return value isn't used for anything that would cause stale display. This is at most a minor code style issue, not a bug that causes stale members to be displayed.
